nameStory: The 'small round-leaved orchid' gets its straightforward name from its most obvious features - it's a petite orchid with distinctively rounded leaves. Unlike many orchids that have long, narrow leaves, this little beauty sports leaves that are almost perfectly circular, making it easy to spot among other woodland plants.
description: The small round-leaved orchid is a tiny woodland treasure, standing just 4-10 inches tall when in bloom. This delicate perennial has one or two rounded, basal leaves that lie flat against the ground and a slender flowering spike topped with small, white to pinkish flowers. It's a succulent plant, meaning its leaves and stems store water, giving them a slightly thick, fleshy feel. This is one of our most northern orchids, preferring cool, moist conditions.

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: One or two perfectly round to oval leaves that lie flat on the ground, feeling thick and slightly succulent to the touch, often with a bluish-green color

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Small white to pale pink orchid flowers arranged in a loose spike, each flower less than half an inch across with the typical orchid lip and spur

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Tiny stature of 4-10 inches tall with a single thin flowering stem rising from the basal leaves

idTips.label: Texture
idTips.description: Leaves feel noticeably thick and fleshy when gently squeezed, unlike most other woodland plants

habitat: This orchid favors cool, moist coniferous and mixed forests, often growing in mossy areas or near bogs and swamps. In New England, it's most likely to be found in northern regions with acidic, organic-rich soils, particularly in areas that stay consistently moist. It often grows alongside sphagnum moss, wild ginger, and other acid-loving plants in shaded woodland settings.

seasonality.spring: Rounded leaves emerge and lie flat against the ground, often appearing before many other woodland plants leaf out.
seasonality.summer: Flowering occurs in mid to late summer (July-August), with the delicate white to pink flower spike rising above the basal leaves.
seasonality.fall: Leaves may persist into early fall before dying back, sometimes taking on reddish tints.
seasonality.winter: Plant is completely dormant with no visible above-ground parts, surviving as underground rhizomes.

funFact: This tiny orchid is so tough it grows wild in Greenland and throughout the Arctic, making it one of the world's most cold-hardy orchids - it can survive temperatures that would kill tropical orchids instantly!
confusionNotes: The round, succulent leaves make this orchid quite distinctive, but when not in flower it might be mistaken for small wild ginger leaves. However, wild ginger leaves are heart-shaped rather than truly round, and they're thin rather than succulent-feeling.
contextualKnowledge: With only one recorded observation in New England, this is an extremely rare find in our region, representing the southern edge of its range. Most orchid enthusiasts in New England will never encounter this species, as it's much more common in Canada and the far northern United States.
compareHints: Unlike its only genus relative in our region, the showy orchis, the small round-leaved orchid has perfectly round basal leaves rather than the oval, upright leaves of showy orchis. The flowers are also much smaller and appear later in summer, while showy orchis blooms in spring with larger, more colorful pink and white flowers.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Showy orchis is much more colorful and compact than its relative the small round-leaved orchid, which has tiny greenish-white flowers and grows in completely different boggy, acidic habitats.
